```yaml title="testing.yaml"
  # Use a block when you need several statements
  - bump --by 2: |
      assert result.exit_code == 0
      assert result_text == "3"

  # Usage errors exit with code 2
  - bump --by nope: assert result.exit_code == 2

  # An uncaught exception is stored on the result
  - crash: |
      assert result.exit_code == 1
      assert isinstance(result.exception, ValueError)

  - "> rm -f counter.*"
```

<!-- docs/guides/dev-loop.md -->

# Hot-reload dev loop

While you are writing a manifest, there are three ways to try your changes. They differ in how much
they install.

| Command | Installs the CLI | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `cli run notes.yaml -- <args>` | no | A quick one-off call. |
| `cli load notes.yaml`, then `cli update notes` | yes | Using the CLI by name; reload by hand. |
| `cli dev notes.yaml` | yes | Reloading automatically on every save. |

## `cli dev`

```console
$ cli dev notes.yaml
🔄 Watching notes.yaml for changes...
```

Leave this running and edit the manifest. Each time you save, cliffy regenerates and reloads the
CLI:

```console
✨ Reloaded notes CLI v0.1.0 ✨
```

In a second terminal, with the same environment active, the `notes` command always reflects the
last save. Stop the watcher with Ctrl+C.

The watcher follows every file the CLI is generated from: the manifest, the manifests it lists under
[`includes`](includes.md) and, for a file written in a [blueprint](../blueprints.md)'s spec, the
blueprint's Python file. Saving any of them reloads the CLI.

!!! note
    Nothing is loaded until the first change. Save the file once, or run `cli load notes.yaml`
    before starting, to get the command right away.

### Run a command on every reload

`--run-cli` runs your CLI after each reload with the arguments that follow. It is a quick way to
re-check one command while you work on it:

```console
$ cli dev notes.yaml --run-cli tags list
🔄 Watching notes.yaml for changes...

✨ Reloaded notes CLI v0.1.0 ✨
general (1)
travel (1)
```

Put `--` before the arguments when they include options:

```console
$ cli dev notes.yaml --run-cli -- list --tag home
$ cli dev notes.yaml --run-cli -- --help
```

A mistake in the manifest prints an error in the watcher's terminal. Fix the file and save again;
the watcher keeps running.

## Managing loaded CLIs

```console
$ cli list            # what is loaded, from which manifest, and how long ago
$ cli info notes      # version, requirements and the stored manifest
$ cli update notes    # regenerate from the manifest path recorded at load time
$ cli remove notes    # uninstall
$ cli remove-all      # uninstall everything cliffy loaded
```

`cli ls`, `cli reload`, `cli rm` and `cli rm-all` are aliases for these. Details are in the
[CLI reference](../reference/cli.md).

Loading writes a small launcher script named after the CLI into the `bin` directory of the
environment. cliffy only replaces or deletes that file while it is exactly the launcher it wrote. If
a file with the name of your CLI is already there (`pip`, say), `cli load` stops and asks you to
rename the CLI. If you edited the launcher, `cli remove` removes nothing, tells you which file is in
the way and leaves the CLI loaded and working; move or delete that file and remove the CLI again.

While `cli dev` runs, reloads happen one at a time and each one reads the manifest when it starts,
so after a burst of saves the loaded CLI is the one of the last save.

Loaded CLIs belong to the Python environment cliffy is installed in. They are available whenever
that environment is active and disappear with it.

<!-- docs/guides/building.md -->

# Building executables

`cli build` turns a manifest into one file that you can hand to someone else. The manifest stays the
same; `--target` chooses what kind of file you get.

| | `zipapp` (default) | `script` | `native` |
|---|---|---|---|
| What you get | `notes`, a Python [zipapp](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipapp.html) with the dependencies inside | `notes.py`, readable Python with the dependencies declared at the top | `notes`, a compiled executable with its own Python inside |
| The other machine needs | A compatible Python | [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), or Python with the dependencies installed | Nothing. Same operating system and CPU as the build machine |
| Network on the other machine | No | The first run, to download the dependencies | No |
| The build machine needs | Network or a pip cache for the dependencies | Nothing | [Rust](https://rustup.rs) (`cargo`), uv and network |
| Build time | 2 s | Under 1 s | 1 min |
| File size | 1.8 MB | 1 to 12 kB | 30 MB |
| First start | 0.2 s | 0.2 s with the dependencies in uv's cache | 1.5 s |
| Later starts | 0.05 s | 0.05 s | 0.05 s |
| Written to disk on the other machine | 8 MB in `~/.shiv` | uv's cache | 110 MB in the user's data and cache directories |

The numbers were measured on an Apple Silicon Mac with Python 3.11 for a CLI whose only dependency is
Typer. They show the proportions; yours will differ.

Whatever the target, the file holds the generated CLI and does not need cliffy. `$` lines with pipes,
redirects or `&&` use a small helper from pybash; `cli build` copies it into the file, so pybash is
not needed either.

## Build

```console
$ cli build notes.yaml -o dist
+ notes built 📦
  dist/notes (single file, needs Python >=3.10, 1.8 MB)
  run it with: ./dist/notes
$ ./dist/notes --version
notes, 0.1.0
```

Without `-o`, the file is written to the current directory. Several manifests can be built in one
call, and a CLI that is already loaded can be built by name:

```console
$ cli build notes.yaml hello.yaml -o dist
$ cli build notes -o dist --target script
```

When a build fails, the reason is printed and `cli build` exits with 1.

A file written in a [blueprint](../blueprints.md#building-a-single-file-executable)'s spec is built
the same way for every target; the blueprint is applied at build time and is not shipped.

## Dependencies

Every target ships the packages under `requires`:

```yaml
requires:
  - tabulate>=0.9.0
```

Unlike `cli load`, building from a manifest does not need those packages to be installed in your
environment.

The framework the generated code imports (Typer, or rich-click with `use_click`) is added for you,
pinned to the version installed next to cliffy unless `requires` names it.

## zipapp

The default. A zipapp built with [shiv](https://shiv.readthedocs.io/) contains the CLI and its
dependencies, downloaded with pip at build time. The other machine needs Python and nothing else.

- The line printed after a build says which Python the file needs. The file checks this when it
  starts and stops with a readable message on an unsupported interpreter.
- The file starts with a `#!` line that selects the Python to run it, `/usr/bin/env python3` by
  default. Change it with `--python`:

    ```console
    $ cli build notes.yaml -o dist --python "/usr/bin/env python3.12"
    ```

- Packages with compiled code are bundled for the platform and Python version you build on. Build
  on the same kind of system you will run on, or stick to pure-Python dependencies.
- Building the same manifest twice in the same environment gives an identical file.
- On first run, shiv unpacks the bundled packages to `~/.shiv`. Set the `SHIV_ROOT` environment
  variable to use another directory.

## script

```console
$ cli build notes.yaml -o dist --target script
+ notes built 📦
  dist/notes.py (single file, needs uv, or Python >=3.11 with typer==0.27.3 installed, 3.6 kB)
  run it with: ./dist/notes.py (or: uv run dist/notes.py)
  uv downloads the dependencies the first time the script runs
```

The result is the Python that `cli render` shows, with three things in front of it: a `#!` line, the
dependencies as [inline script metadata](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/inline-script-metadata/)
and a check of the Python version.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#     "typer==0.27.3",
# ]
# ///
```

- With uv installed, `./dist/notes.py` and `uv run dist/notes.py` both work. uv creates an environment
  with exactly the listed dependencies, downloads them on the first run and reuses them afterwards.
- Without uv, install the dependencies yourself and run `python dist/notes.py`.
- Nothing is downloaded at build time, so the build works offline and gives the same file every time.
- The file is plain text: it can be read, reviewed in a diff and edited. This is the target to pick
  when the reader should see what they run.
- `--python` replaces the `#!` line, for example `--python "/usr/bin/env python3"` for machines
  without uv.

## native

```console
$ cli build notes.yaml -o dist --target native
+ notes built 📦
  dist/notes (single file, needs nothing installed, runs on macOS arm64, 30.1 MB)
  run it with: ./dist/notes
  the first run unpacks its Python 3.11 (75.0 MB) into the user's data directory, without network access; later runs start right away
```

The result is one compiled executable. It contains a complete Python with the CLI and its
dependencies already installed, so the other machine needs neither Python nor network access.

### What the build machine needs

- **Rust.** `cargo` compiles the launcher. Install it from [rustup.rs](https://rustup.rs).
- **uv.** It downloads the standalone Python and installs the CLI into it. See
  [Installing uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).
- **Network access**, for that Python, the dependencies and the source of the launcher.
- About a minute, and 700 MB of temporary disk space that is freed when the build ends.

When `cargo` or `uv` is missing, `cli build` says so and how to install it before it starts.

### How it is built

1. uv downloads a [standalone Python](https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone) of the
   version cliffy runs on.
2. The generated CLI is packaged as a wheel and installed into that Python together with its
   dependencies.
3. The result is embedded in [PyApp](https://ofek.dev/pyapp/), a launcher written in Rust, which is
   compiled into the executable.

### What happens on the other machine

- The executable runs on the operating system and CPU architecture it was built on. Build on each
  platform you want to support. The target is available on macOS and Linux.
- The first run unpacks the embedded Python, which takes a second or two, and then starts the CLI.
  Nothing is downloaded and nothing is installed with pip. Later runs only check that the directory
  exists.
- The Python is unpacked to `pyapp/<name>` in the user's data directory
  (`~/Library/Application Support` on macOS, `~/.local/share` on Linux), and a copy of the archive is
  kept in the cache directory (`~/Library/Caches/pyapp`, `~/.cache/pyapp`). Together that is about
  110 MB for a small CLI. Set `PYAPP_INSTALL_DIR_<NAME>`, with the name of the CLI in upper case, to
  unpack somewhere else. Delete the directory to reclaim the space; the next run unpacks it again.
- Every argument goes to your CLI. PyApp's own `self` commands are turned off.

`--python` does not apply to this target.

## Things that hold for every target

- Values taken from `env` in `vars` are fixed at build time. See
  [Vars and Jinja](vars-and-jinja.md#environment-variables).
- External commands that the CLI runs with `$` lines are not bundled. They have to exist on the
  other machine.

## Check before you ship

```console
$ cli test notes.yaml
$ cli build notes.yaml -o dist
$ ./dist/notes --help
```

<!-- docs/guides/generating-docs.md -->

# Generating docs

`cli docs` writes a reference page for your CLI from its manifest: the description, every command
with its params and aliases, and the examples you provide.

## Add examples

`examples` is a list of command lines with a description each. They are part of the documentation
`cli docs` writes, and the generated CLI shows them at the end of its own `--help`:

```text
 Examples:

 $ notes add "buy milk" --tag home  # Add a note tagged home.

 $ notes ls --tag home  # Show only the notes tagged home.
```

Write an example as you would type it, starting with the name of the CLI. It is shown as written:
quotes, brackets and backslashes are not interpreted. The help of a single command does not repeat
the examples.

```yaml
examples:
  - command: notes add "buy milk" --tag home
    description: Add a note tagged home.
  - command: notes ls --tag home
    description: Show only the notes tagged home.
```

Give every example a `description`. A plain string is accepted too, but is rendered with `None` in
place of the description.

## Generate

```console
$ cli docs notes.yaml
+ notes.md
```

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--format`, `-f` | `md`, `rst`, `html` | `md` |
| `--output-dir`, `-o` | an existing directory | the current directory |

```console
$ mkdir -p site
$ cli docs notes.yaml --format html --output-dir site
+ notes.html
```

## What the page contains

For the `notes` manifest from the [Quickstart](../quickstart.md), the Markdown output starts like
this:

````markdown
# notes v0.1.0

Keep short notes in a JSON file

## Commands

### add
Add a note

Parameters:
- text: Text
- tag: Tag

### list|ls
List notes, optionally filtered by tag

Parameters:
- --tag: str (default: "")

Aliases: ls
````

and ends with the examples:

````markdown
## Examples

```bash
notes add "buy milk" --tag home
```
Add a note tagged home.
````

- Commands are listed in manifest order, under the key they have in the manifest.
- Shorthand and explicit params are listed with their type; explicit params also show their help
  text. Generic params (plain strings) are left out.
- Pass a manifest path or the name of a loaded CLI. A loaded CLI is documented from the manifest path
  recorded by `cli load`.

<!-- docs/blueprints.md -->

# Blueprints

A cliffy manifest describes a CLI in cliffy's own vocabulary: `commands`, `params`, `run`. A **blueprint** lets you
bring your own vocabulary instead. You define the YAML schema that fits your domain and tell cliffy how it maps
onto a CLI. Files written in that schema then work with `cli load`, `cli run`, `cli render`, `cli test`, `cli dev`,
`cli docs` and `cli build`, which turns them into a single-file executable.

```
your YAML spec ──▶ Blueprint (validate, to_manifest) ──▶ cliffy manifest ──▶ Typer or Click code ──▶ one executable file
```

## Writing a blueprint

A blueprint is a [pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev) model with one required method. The fields are your schema,
and `to_manifest` returns the cliffy manifest for a validated file.

```python title="tasks.py"
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from cliffy.blueprint import Blueprint
from cliffy.manifest import CLIManifest, Command, RunBlock


class Task(BaseModel):
    run: str | list[str] = Field(description="Shell line(s) to run, in order.")
    help: str = Field(default="", description="What the task does, shown in --help.")


class Tasks(Blueprint):
    """Task runner: every entry under `tasks` becomes a command that runs shell lines"""

    name: str = Field(description="Name of the CLI.")
    version: str = Field(default="0.1.0", description="Version of the CLI.")
    help: str = Field(default="", description="Description of the CLI.")
    tasks: dict[str, str | list[str] | Task] = Field(min_length=1, description="Tasks by name.")

    def to_manifest(self) -> CLIManifest:
        commands = {}
        for name, entry in self.tasks.items():
            task = entry if isinstance(entry, Task) else Task(run=entry)
            lines = [task.run] if isinstance(task.run, str) else task.run
            script = "\n".join(f"subprocess.run({line!r}, shell=True, check=True)" for line in lines)
            commands[name] = Command(help=task.help, run=RunBlock(script))

        return CLIManifest(name=self.name, version=self.version, help=self.help, commands=commands)
```

A file written in that spec names its blueprint with a top-level `blueprint:` key:

```yaml title="tasks.yaml"
blueprint: tasks.py

name: tasks
help: Project tasks

tasks:
  greet: echo "hello from tasks"
  check:
    - echo "linting"
    - echo "testing"
  release:
    help: Check, then tag the release
    run:
      - echo "linting"
      - echo "tagging"
```

```
$ cli run tasks.yaml -- greet
hello from tasks

$ cli load tasks.yaml
$ tasks check
linting
testing
```

`to_manifest` may return a `CLIManifest` or a plain mapping that validates as one. Because the result is an
ordinary manifest, everything cliffy does with manifests applies: both the Typer and the Click generator
(`use_click`), `requires`, `tests`, command aliases, callbacks and so on.

The whole file is rendered with Jinja2 before the blueprint sees it, exactly like a manifest.

## Selecting a blueprint

Either in the file, or on the command line. The command line wins.

```yaml
blueprint: tasks.py
```

```
cli run jobs.yaml --blueprint tasks.py -- greet
```

`--blueprint` / `-b` is available on `load`, `run`, `render`, `build`, `dev`, `test`, `validate` and `docs`.
`cli update` reuses the blueprint a CLI was loaded with, and `cli info` shows it.

A blueprint reference is one of:

| Reference | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tasks.py`, `./bp/tasks.py:Tasks` | A Python file. In a YAML file the path is relative to that file; on the command line it is relative to the working directory. Add `:ClassName` when the file defines several blueprints. |
| `mypackage.blueprints:Tasks` | An importable class. `mypackage.blueprints` alone works when the module defines exactly one blueprint. |
| `tasks` | A blueprint provided by an installed package (see [Sharing blueprints](#sharing-blueprints)). |

Cliffy reports a reference it cannot use and says why: the file or module does not exist, the name is provided by
more than one package, the module defines no blueprint or more than one, or the target is not a blueprint.

## Validation errors

Unknown keys are rejected by default, so typos are caught. Errors are reported against your spec, with the path
to the offending key:

```
$ cli validate server.yaml
~ server.yaml is not a valid MCPTools spec
  tools[0].name: Value error, `serve` is a reserved name (got 'serve')
  tools[1].parameters[0].type: Input should be 'string', 'integer', 'number', 'boolean' or 'array' (got 'strng')
  tols: Extra inputs are not permitted 💔
```

Use pydantic validators for rules that go beyond types. To accept unknown keys, set
`model_config = ConfigDict(extra="ignore")` on your blueprint.

## Hooks

Three optional hooks run around `to_manifest`:

```
pre_validate(raw) ──▶ validation ──▶ to_manifest() ──▶ post_manifest(manifest) ──▶ code generation ──▶ post_codegen(code)
```

| Hook | Receives | Use it to |
|---|---|---|
| `pre_validate(cls, raw)` (classmethod) | The YAML mapping, without the `blueprint` key | Accept shorthand forms, set defaults, rename legacy keys |
| `post_manifest(self, manifest)` | The `CLIManifest` | Adjust the manifest, i.e. add commands every CLI of this kind gets |
| `post_codegen(self, code)` | The generated Python source | Adjust the generated code, i.e. prepend a license header |

```python
class Tasks(Blueprint):
    ...

    @classmethod
    def pre_validate(cls, raw):
        # allow `jobs:` as an older name for `tasks:`
        if "jobs" in raw:
            raw = {**raw, "tasks": raw.pop("jobs")}
        return raw

    def post_codegen(self, code):
        return "# generated from a Tasks spec, do not edit\n" + code
```

## Editor completion

`cli blueprint schema` prints the JSON schema of a blueprint's spec.

```
cli blueprint schema tasks.py -o tasks.schema.json
```

Reference it from your YAML files to get validation and completion from the YAML language server:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=tasks.schema.json
blueprint: tasks.py
```

Field descriptions (`Field(description=...)`) show up as hover documentation.

## Building a single-file executable

`cli build` applies the blueprint at build time and bundles the generated CLI with its dependencies into one
executable [zipapp](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipapp.html). With `--target script` or `--target native`
the same file becomes a single Python script or a compiled executable instead; see
[Building executables](guides/building.md).

```
$ cli build tasks.yaml -o dist
+ tasks built 📦
  dist/tasks (single file, needs Python >=3.10, 1.8 MB)
  run it with: ./dist/tasks

$ ./dist/tasks greet
hello from tasks
```

The file runs on any machine with a matching Python. It does not need cliffy, the blueprint, pydantic or the YAML
file.

* **Dependencies.** Whatever the manifest lists under `requires` is bundled. Let your blueprint set `requires`
  for the packages its generated code imports. The CLI framework (typer, or rich-click with `use_click`) is added
  automatically, pinned to the version installed next to cliffy unless `requires` names it.
* **Interpreter.** `--python` / `-p` sets the shebang, by default `/usr/bin/env python3`. The build reports which
  Python versions the bundle supports. A bundle of pure-Python packages runs on every version its packages accept.
  A bundle with compiled extensions only runs on the Python minor version it was built with, so build with the
  version you deploy to. Started with an unsupported Python, the executable exits with a message that says so.
* **Reproducible.** Building the same input twice with the same package versions gives a byte-identical file.
* **Errors.** When a dependency cannot be installed, the build prints pip's reason and writes no file.

On first run the executable unpacks its packages into `~/.shiv` (set `SHIV_ROOT` to change the location).

## Sharing blueprints

A package can register blueprints under the `cliffy.blueprints` entry-point group:

```toml title="pyproject.toml"
[project.entry-points."cliffy.blueprints"]
tasks = "mypackage.blueprints:Tasks"
```

Once the package is installed, the blueprint is available by name:

```yaml
blueprint: tasks
```

```
$ cli blueprints
┏━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ Name  ┃ Blueprint                  ┃ Package   ┃ Description                       ┃
┡━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ tasks │ mypackage.blueprints:Tasks │ mypackage │ Task runner: every entry under... │
└───────┴────────────────────────────┴───────────┴───────────────────────────────────┘
```

`cli blueprints` is short for `cli blueprint list`. The description is the first line of the class docstring.

## Examples

Two worked examples live in [`examples/blueprints`](https://github.com/jaykv/cliffy/tree/main/examples/blueprints):

* `tasks.py` with `tasks.yaml`: the task runner from this page.
* `mcp_tools.py` with `text-tools.yaml`: an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) tool server. The spec lists
  tools with typed parameters and a Python body. The generated CLI has one command per tool, a `tools` command
  that prints the tool definitions, and a `serve` command that speaks MCP over stdio without extra dependencies.
  `cli build examples/blueprints/text-tools.yaml` gives a single file you can register as an MCP server.

## Callbacks

Callbacks are a manifest feature that blueprints often need: code that runs before every command of the CLI, or
of one command group. They work with both Typer and Click, and the built-in `--version` and `--aliases` options
stay in place.

```yaml
callbacks:
  # no `group`: runs before every command, its params become options of the CLI itself
  - params:
      - name: --verbose
        type: bool
        default: false
        short: -v
        help: Print what is about to run
    invoke_without_command: true
    run: |
      ctx.obj = {"verbose": verbose}
      if ctx.invoked_subcommand is None:
          print("no command given, try --help")
      elif verbose:
          print(f"running {ctx.invoked_subcommand}")

  # runs before every command of the `db` group
  - group: db
    run: print("connecting to db")

commands:
  hello: print("hello")
  db.migrate: print("migrating")
```

```
$ mycli --verbose db migrate
running db
connecting to db
migrating
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `run` | Code to run. The Typer or Click context is available as `ctx`. |
| `group` | Command group the callback belongs to, i.e. `db` or `db.tables`. Leave it out for the CLI itself. |
| `params` | Options given before the command name, in the same syntax as command params. |
| `invoke_without_command` | Also run when no command is given, instead of showing the help. |

Several callbacks for the same target run in the order given. A manifest with only callbacks and no `commands`
is valid, which makes a single-purpose CLI.

<!-- docs/ai.md -->

# AI commands

Cliffy includes AI-powered commands that generate manifests and answer questions about cliffy. They live in the `cli ai` command group; every option is listed in the [CLI reference](reference/cli.md#cli-ai).

The AI commands are a convenience. Nothing else in cliffy needs a model: a manifest written by hand, or by an agent from the [manifest schema](reference/manifest.md), works the same way.

!!! note
    Requires the `ai` extra: `pip install "cliffy[ai]"`. See [Installation](installation.md#extras).
    Without it, `cli ai` commands exit with an install hint; the rest of cliffy is unaffected.

## Choosing a model

The AI commands are built on [Pydantic AI](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/overview/) and work with any model it supports. Models are named `provider:model`, and each provider reads its API key from its usual environment variable.

The model is picked in this order:

1. the `--model` / `-m` option
2. the `CLIFFY_AI_MODEL` environment variable
3. a default for the first provider that has an API key set:

    | API key | Default model |
    |---|---|
    | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` (or `GEMINI_API_KEY`) | `google:gemini-flash-latest` |
    | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5` |
    | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `openai:gpt-5.4-mini` |

```bash
# use the default model of the provider whose key is set
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='your-api-key'
cli ai generate mycli "Create a todo app"

# pick a model for one command
cli ai generate mycli "Create a todo app" --model openai:gpt-5.5

# or for the whole shell session
export CLIFFY_AI_MODEL=google:gemini-2.5-pro
```

!!! tip
    Use `--preview` to print the fully constructed prompt instead of sending it. This needs neither a model nor an API key.

## Generating a manifest

Generate complete CLI manifests from natural language descriptions:

```bash
cli ai generate mycli "Create a CLI for managing docker containers with commands to list, start, stop and remove containers"
cli load mycli.yaml
```

The model's reply is validated before anything is written: it has to be valid YAML, match the manifest schema, and produce a CLI that is valid Python. A reply that fails is sent back to the model together with the reason, up to `--retries` times (default 2). If no valid manifest comes back, the command fails and writes nothing.

`mycli.yaml` is written to the current directory, or to `--output-dir`. An existing file is only replaced with `--force`.

!!! warning
    Validation checks that the manifest loads, not that the commands do what you asked. Read the generated run blocks before running the CLI.

## Asking questions

Get AI assistance for understanding and working with cliffy:

```bash
cli ai ask "How do I create nested subcommands?"
```

The question is answered from a reference built from your installed cliffy version: its command list, the annotated `cli init` template and the manifest JSON schema.

You can also get targeted help about specific CLIs by referencing a manifest or a loaded CLI:

```bash
cli ai ask --cli mycli.yaml "How do I add input validation to the start command?"
```

The answer is printed to stdout and token usage to stderr, so the answer can be redirected to a file.

## Giving cliffy's documentation to an agent

`cli ai llms-txt` prints cliffy's documentation as a single text file in the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) layout: the quickstart, the guides and the CLI and manifest references.

```bash
cli ai llms-txt > cliffy-llms.txt
```

The file is bundled with the installed package, so it needs no network access, no model and no `ai` extra, and it always describes the version you have installed. Put it in the context of a coding agent and it can write and fix manifests without looking anything up.

The same file is published with the documentation at [`/llms.txt`](llms.txt).

# CLI reference

Installing cliffy adds two identical entry points, `cli` and `cliffy`. This page uses `cli`.
It is generated from the command definitions in `cliffy/cli.py` and `cliffy/ai.py`, so the
arguments, options and defaults below are the ones the installed version accepts.

```text
cli [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

## Commands at a glance

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| [`cli ai`](#cli-ai) | AI-powered commands. `generate` and `ask` require the `ai` extra: pip install 'cliffy[ai]' |
| [`cli blueprint`](#cli-blueprint) | Work with blueprints: custom YAML specs that map onto a CLI |
| [`cli build`](#cli-build) | Build a CLI manifest or a loaded CLI into a single file to hand to someone else |
| [`cli dev`](#cli-dev) | Start hot-reloader for a manifest for active development. |
| [`cli docs`](#cli-docs) | Generate documentation for a CLI |
| [`cli info`](#cli-info) | Display CLI info |
| [`cli init`](#cli-init) | Generate a CLI manifest template |
| [`cli list`](#cli-list) | List all CLIs loaded |
| [`cli load`](#cli-load) | Load CLI for given manifest(s) |
| [`cli remove`](#cli-remove) | Remove a loaded CLI by name |
| [`cli remove-all`](#cli-remove-all) | Remove all loaded CLIs |
| [`cli render`](#cli-render) | Render the CLI manifest generation as code |
| [`cli run`](#cli-run) | Run CLI for a manifest |
| [`cli test`](#cli-test) | Run tests defined in a manifest |
| [`cli update`](#cli-update) | Reloads CLI by name |
| [`cli validate`](#cli-validate) | Validate a CLI manifest: its structure, its requirements and the code generated from it |

## Global options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--version` | Print the version and exit. |
| `--aliases` | List the command aliases and exit. |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show help. Every command accepts this option. |

## Aliases

Aliases are hidden from `cli --help`. `cli --aliases` prints this list.

| Alias | Command |
|---|---|
| `cli ls` | [`cli list`](#cli-list) |
| `cli add` | [`cli load`](#cli-load) |
| `cli reload` | [`cli update`](#cli-update) |
| `cli rm` | [`cli remove`](#cli-remove) |
| `cli rm-all` | [`cli remove-all`](#cli-remove-all) |
| `cli rmall` | [`cli remove-all`](#cli-remove-all) |
| `cli blueprints` | [`cli blueprint list`](#cli-blueprint-list) |

## `cli ai`

AI-powered commands. `generate` and `ask` require the `ai` extra: pip install 'cliffy[ai]'

```text
cli ai [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

`generate` and `ask` need the `ai` extra (`pip install "cliffy[ai]"`). Both send the manifest JSON
schema to the model as part of the prompt and print token usage when they finish. `llms-txt` needs no
extra and calls no model.

Model names use the pydantic-ai `provider:model` form, and the API key of that provider must be set in
the environment. Without `--model`, the `CLIFFY_AI_MODEL` environment variable is used, then a default
for the first provider that has an API key set. See [AI commands](../ai.md).

### `cli ai ask`

Ask a question about cliffy or a specific CLI manifest.

```text
cli ai ask [OPTIONS] PROMPT
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PROMPT` | text | yes |  | Your question. |
| `--preview` | flag | no |  | Print the prompt instead of sending it. Needs no model. |
| `--max-tokens` | integer range | no |  | Maximum number of tokens in a model response. |
| `-m`, `--model` | text | no |  | Model to use, as `provider:model`. See https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/overview/. Defaults to a model of the first provider with an API key set, else google:gemini-flash-latest. |
| `--cli` | file | no |  | Loaded CLI or manifest to include in the prompt as reference. |

`--preview` prints the prompt and exits without calling a model.

### `cli ai generate`

Generate a CLI manifest based on a description.

```text
cli ai generate [OPTIONS] CLI_NAME DESCRIPTION
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CLI_NAME` | text | yes |  | Name of the CLI. The manifest is written to `<cli_name>.yaml`. |
| `DESCRIPTION` | text | yes |  | Plain-language description of the CLI you want. |
| `--preview` | flag | no |  | Print the prompt instead of sending it. Needs no model. |
| `--max-tokens` | integer range | no |  | Maximum number of tokens in a model response. |
| `-m`, `--model` | text | no |  | Model to use, as `provider:model`. See https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/overview/. Defaults to a model of the first provider with an API key set, else google:gemini-flash-latest. |
| `--retries` | integer range | no | `2` | How often to send an invalid manifest back to the model to be fixed. |
| `-f`, `--force` | flag | no |  | Overwrite the manifest file if it exists. |
| `-o`, `--output-dir` | directory | no | `.` | Output directory |

The reply of the model is validated before the manifest is written, and sent back with the reason when
it is not a manifest cliffy can load. `--preview` prints the prompt and exits without calling a model.

### `cli ai llms-txt`

Print the bundled cliffy documentation as llms.txt. Needs no model.

```text
cli ai llms-txt [OPTIONS]
```

Prints the documentation that is bundled with the installed cliffy as one text file, in the
[llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) layout. It needs no model, no API key and no `ai` extra, so it works
offline and always matches the installed version.

```console
$ cli ai llms-txt > cliffy-llms.txt
$ cli ai llms-txt | pbcopy
```

Give the output to a coding agent, or add it to a project's context, so that it can write manifests
without looking anything up.

## `cli blueprint`

Work with blueprints: custom YAML specs that map onto a CLI

```text
cli blueprint [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

A blueprint lets a YAML file use its own keys instead of `commands` and `params`, and maps them onto a
CLI. See [Blueprints](../blueprints.md).

### `cli blueprint list`

List the blueprints provided by installed packages

```text
cli blueprint list [OPTIONS]
```

Alias: `cli blueprints`

Lists the blueprints that installed packages register under the `cliffy.blueprints` entry point group.
A blueprint in a `.py` file or referenced as `module:Class` works without being listed.

```console
$ cli blueprint list
No blueprints installed. Use a .py file or module:Class reference, or install a blueprint package.
```

### `cli blueprint schema`

Print the JSON schema of a blueprint's spec, for validation and editor completion

```text
cli blueprint schema [OPTIONS] BLUEPRINT
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BLUEPRINT` | text | yes |  | Blueprint reference: a `.py` file, `module:Class` or the name of an installed blueprint. |
| `-o`, `--output` | file | no |  | Write the schema to a file |

```console
$ cli blueprint schema examples/blueprints/tasks.py -o tasks.schema.json
+ tasks.schema.json
```

Point a `# yaml-language-server: $schema=` comment at the file to get completion and validation for
files written in the blueprint's spec.

## `cli build`

Build a CLI manifest or a loaded CLI into a single file to hand to someone else

```text
cli build [OPTIONS] [CLI_OR_MANIFESTS]...
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[CLI_OR_MANIFESTS]...` | file | no |  | Manifest files (paths ending in `yaml`) or names of loaded CLIs. |
| `-t`, `--target` | `zipapp` \| `script` \| `native` | no | `zipapp` | What to build: `zipapp` is a zipapp with its dependencies bundled, which needs a compatible Python; `script` is a .py script that declares its dependencies inline, which needs uv or an environment with them; `native` is a compiled executable that brings its own Python and needs nothing installed (built with cargo and uv). |
| `-o`, `--output-dir` | directory | no |  | Output dir |
| `-p`, `--python` | text | no |  | Interpreter for the #! line of a zipapp or a script, added after the #!. [default: /usr/bin/env python3 for a zipapp, /usr/bin/env -S uv run --script for a script] |
| `-b`, `--blueprint` | text | no |  | Blueprint that maps a custom YAML spec onto a CLI: a .py file, module:Class or an installed blueprint name. Overrides the `blueprint:` key of the file. |

Builds one file to hand to someone else. `--target` chooses what kind:

| Target | What you get | Needs on the other machine |
|---|---|---|
| `zipapp` | `hello`, a [zipapp](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipapp.html) built with [shiv](https://shiv.readthedocs.io/) that contains the dependencies | A compatible Python |
| `script` | `hello.py`, a script with its dependencies declared inline | [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), or Python with the dependencies installed |
| `native` | `hello`, a compiled executable with its own Python | Nothing |

Every target ships the generated CLI, the framework it imports (Typer, or rich-click with
`use_click`) and every package listed under `requires`. Without `--output-dir` the file is written
to the current directory.

```console
$ cli build hello.yaml -o dist
+ hello built 📦
  dist/hello (single file, needs Python >=3.10, 1.8 MB)
  run it with: ./dist/hello
$ ./dist/hello greet Ada
Hello, Ada!
$ cli build hello.yaml -o dist --target script
+ hello built 📦
  dist/hello.py (single file, needs uv, or Python >=3.11 with typer==0.27.3 installed, 1.3 kB)
  run it with: ./dist/hello.py (or: uv run dist/hello.py)
  uv downloads the dependencies the first time the script runs
```

The `native` target needs `cargo` and `uv` on the machine that builds. When a build fails, the
reason is printed and the exit code is `1`. With `--blueprint`, or a `blueprint:` key in the file,
the blueprint is applied at build time and is not needed to run the result.

See [Building executables](../guides/building.md).

## `cli dev`

Start hot-reloader for a manifest for active development.

Examples:

- cli dev examples/hello.yaml

- cli dev examples/hello.yaml --run-cli  -- -h

- cli dev examples/hello.yaml --run-cli python

```text
cli dev [OPTIONS] MANIFEST [RUN_CLI_ARGS]...
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MANIFEST` | file | yes |  | Manifest file to watch. |
| `[RUN_CLI_ARGS]...` | text | no |  | Arguments for the generated CLI when `--run-cli` is set. |
| `--run-cli` | flag | no |  | If passed, runs CLI on each reload. Useful for syntax checks or testing command execution on each reload |
| `-b`, `--blueprint` | text | no |  | Blueprint that maps a custom YAML spec onto a CLI: a .py file, module:Class or an installed blueprint name. Overrides the `blueprint:` key of the file. |

Nothing is loaded when the command starts. The CLI is loaded the first time the file changes and
again on every later change. The manifests it includes and the Python file of its blueprint are
watched too. Stop with Ctrl+C.

With `--run-cli`, the remaining arguments are passed to the freshly generated CLI after each reload.
Put `--` before them when they include options.

See [Hot-reload dev loop](../guides/dev-loop.md).

## `cli docs`

Generate documentation for a CLI

```text
cli docs [OPTIONS] CLI_OR_MANIFEST
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CLI_OR_MANIFEST` | file | yes |  | Manifest file (a path ending in `yaml`) or the name of a loaded CLI. |
| `-f`, `--format` | `md` \| `rst` \| `html` | no | `md` | Output format. |
| `-o`, `--output-dir` | directory | no |  | Output directory |
| `-b`, `--blueprint` | text | no |  | Blueprint that maps a custom YAML spec onto a CLI: a .py file, module:Class or an installed blueprint name. Overrides the `blueprint:` key of the file. |

Writes `<name>.md`, `<name>.rst` or `<name>.html` to the output directory, or to the current directory
when `--output-dir` is not given. The output directory must exist.

A loaded CLI is documented from the manifest path recorded by `cli load`.

See [Generating docs](../guides/generating-docs.md).

## `cli info`

Display CLI info

```text
cli info [OPTIONS] CLI_NAME
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CLI_NAME` | text | yes |  | Name of a loaded CLI. |

Prints the name, version, requirements, blueprint (when one was used), age and stored manifest of a
loaded CLI.

## `cli init`

Generate a CLI manifest template

```text
cli init [OPTIONS] [CLI_NAME]
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[CLI_NAME]` | text | no | `mycli` | Name of the CLI. The manifest is written to `<cli_name>.yaml`. |
| `--render` | flag | no |  | Print template to terminal directly |
| `--raw` | flag | no |  | Raw template without boilerplate helpers and examples. |
| `--json-schema` | flag | no |  | Write JSON schema (cliffy_schema.json) file to the current directory. Useful for development. |

```console
$ cli init mycli --raw
+ mycli.yaml
```

`--raw` writes a skeleton with every top-level key, one `hello` command and one test. Without `--raw`
the manifest is a commented tour of the format with example commands. Both run and pass `cli test` as
written.

`--json-schema` also writes `cliffy_schema.json` and adds a `# yaml-language-server` comment that points
at it. See [Editor setup](../guides/editor-setup.md).

## `cli list`

List all CLIs loaded

```text
cli list [OPTIONS]
```

Alias: `cli ls`

```console
$ cli list
┏━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ Name  ┃ Version ┃ Age ┃ Manifest                ┃
┡━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ hello │ 0.1.0   │ 5s  │ /home/ada/hello.yaml    │
└───────┴─────────┴─────┴─────────────────────────┘
```

## `cli load`

Load CLI for given manifest(s)

```text
cli load [OPTIONS] [MANIFESTS]...
```

Alias: `cli add`

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[MANIFESTS]...` | file | no |  | One or more manifest files to load. |
| `-b`, `--blueprint` | text | no |  | Blueprint that maps a custom YAML spec onto a CLI: a .py file, module:Class or an installed blueprint name. Overrides the `blueprint:` key of the file. |

Loading does three things:

1. generates the CLI code and writes it to `cliffy/clis/<name>.py` inside the installed cliffy package,
2. writes a launcher script called `<name>` into the `bin` directory of the Python environment cliffy
   is installed in,
3. records the manifest path and contents so that `cli list`, `cli info` and `cli update` can find it.

The CLI is therefore available wherever that environment is active. Packages listed under `requires`
must already be installed, otherwise loading stops with `missing requirement`.

A file written in a [blueprint](../blueprints.md)'s spec is loaded the same way. The blueprint comes from
`--blueprint` or from the file's `blueprint:` key and is remembered, so `cli update` applies it again.

```console
$ cli load hello.yaml
✨ Generated hello CLI v0.1.0 ✨
$ hello -h
```

See [Hot-reload dev loop](../guides/dev-loop.md).

## `cli remove`

Remove a loaded CLI by name

```text
cli remove [OPTIONS] [CLI_NAMES]...
```

Alias: `cli rm`

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[CLI_NAMES]...` | text | no |  | Names of loaded CLIs to remove. |

Deletes the launcher script, the generated module and the stored metadata.

```console
$ cli remove hello
~ hello removed 💥
```

## `cli remove-all`

Remove all loaded CLIs

```text
cli remove-all [OPTIONS]
```

Aliases: `cli rm-all`, `cli rmall`

## `cli render`

Render the CLI manifest generation as code

```text
cli render [OPTIONS] MANIFEST
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MANIFEST` | file | yes |  | Manifest file to render. |
| `-b`, `--blueprint` | text | no |  | Blueprint that maps a custom YAML spec onto a CLI: a .py file, module:Class or an installed blueprint name. Overrides the `blueprint:` key of the file. |

Prints the Python module cliffy generates, without loading or running it. Use it to see exactly how
params, shell lines and templates are translated.

```console
$ cli render hello.yaml
```

## `cli run`

Run CLI for a manifest

```text
cli run [OPTIONS] MANIFEST [CLI_ARGS]...
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MANIFEST` | file | yes |  | Manifest file to run. |
| `[CLI_ARGS]...` | text | no |  | Arguments passed to the generated CLI. Put `--` first when they include options. |
| `-b`, `--blueprint` | text | no |  | Blueprint that maps a custom YAML spec onto a CLI: a .py file, module:Class or an installed blueprint name. Overrides the `blueprint:` key of the file. |

Generates the CLI in a temporary file and runs it once, without loading it. Options meant for your
CLI must come after `--`, otherwise `cli run` tries to parse them itself:

```console
$ cli run hello.yaml greet Ada
Hello, Ada!
$ cli run hello.yaml -- greet Ada --shout
HELLO, ADA!
$ cli run hello.yaml -- --help
```

Help output shows the temporary file name instead of the CLI name.

## `cli test`

Run tests defined in a manifest

```text
cli test [OPTIONS] MANIFEST
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MANIFEST` | file | yes |  | Manifest file whose `tests` section should run. |
| `-x`, `--exitfirst` | flag | no |  | exit instantly on first error or failed test. |
| `--traceback` | flag | no |  | Also print the full Python traceback of a command that raises. |
| `-b`, `--blueprint` | text | no |  | Blueprint that maps a custom YAML spec onto a CLI: a .py file, module:Class or an installed blueprint name. Overrides the `blueprint:` key of the file. |

Runs the `tests` section of a manifest and prints each command, its output and the result. The exit
code is `0` only when every test passes. It is `1` when a test fails or when the manifest has no tests.

See [Testing manifests](../guides/testing.md).

## `cli update`

Reloads CLI by name

```text
cli update [OPTIONS] [CLI_NAMES]...
```

Alias: `cli reload`

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[CLI_NAMES]...` | text | no |  | Names of loaded CLIs to regenerate from their manifests. |

`update` re-reads the manifest from the path recorded by `cli load`, so it only works while the manifest
is still at that location.

```console
$ cli update hello
✨ Reloaded hello CLI v0.1.0 ✨
$ hello -h
```

## `cli validate`

Validate a CLI manifest: its structure, its requirements and the code generated from it

```text
cli validate [OPTIONS] MANIFEST
```

| Argument or option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MANIFEST` | file | yes |  | Manifest file to validate. |
| `-b`, `--blueprint` | text | no |  | Blueprint that maps a custom YAML spec onto a CLI: a .py file, module:Class or an installed blueprint name. Overrides the `blueprint:` key of the file. |

Checks that the file is valid YAML, matches the manifest schema, that its `requires` are installed and
that the generated code works. Scripts are checked while the code is generated, as they are by every
other command. `validate` then compiles and imports the generated code, which defines the commands
without running any of them. The code in `imports` and `functions` and the expressions in `vars` do run.

```console
$ cli validate hello.yaml
Manifest hello.yaml is valid
```

An error in a script is reported with its command, line and column. A problem that only shows when
the code is imported, such as a type that does not exist, is reported against the command it comes
from:

```console
$ cli validate broken.yaml
~ error in broken.yaml: command `db.create`, run, line 2, column 7: not valid Python: '(' was never closed
    print((
          ^ 💔
$ cli validate other.yaml
Manifest other.yaml is invalid: the generated code does not work
  command `db.create`: NameError: name 'Table' is not defined
    def db_create(table: Table = typer.Argument(...)): 💔
```

<!-- docs/reference/manifest.md -->

  Source: scripts/docs.py. Regenerate with `make docs-generate`.

# Manifest reference

Every key a manifest accepts. The tables are generated from the pydantic models in
`cliffy/manifest.py`, the same models that produce the
[JSON schema](https://github.com/jaykv/cliffy/blob/main/examples/cliffy_schema.json) used for
[editor completion](../guides/editor-setup.md). The notes under each table are written by hand.

## Top-level keys

The top level of a manifest file.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manifestVersion` | string | `"v3"` | Manifest schema version. `v3` is the only version that is read; any other value is an error. |
| `name` | string | **required** | The name of the CLI, used when invoking from command line. |
| `version` | string | **required** | CLI version |
| `help` | string | `""` | Brief description of the CLI |
| `use_click` | boolean | `false` | Generate CLI to Click instead of Typer |
| `requires` | list of strings | `[]` | Python packages the CLI needs, as requirement specifiers such as `rich` or `tabulate>=0.9.0`. Checked when the manifest is loaded and bundled by `cli build`. |
| `includes` | list of strings | `[]` | Paths of other manifest files to merge into this one, relative to this file. Keys set in this manifest win over included ones and lists are combined. When two included files set the same key, the first one listed wins. |
| `vars` | mapping of name to (string or `{expression}`) | `{}` | Variables for the manifest. Each one can be used anywhere in the file as `{{ name }}` and is also defined as a module-level Python variable in the generated CLI. A value is a string, a number, a boolean, or a Python expression written as `{expression}`. String values are Jinja2 templates: they can use other vars, and `env` gives access to environment variables. |
| `imports` | string or list of strings | `[]` | String block or list of strings containing any module imports. These can be used to import any python modules that the CLI depends on. |
| `functions` | string or list of strings | `[]` | String block or list of helper function definitions. These functions should be defined as strings that can be executed by the Python interpreter. |
| `types` | mapping of name to string | `{}` | A mapping containing any shared type definitions. These types can be referenced by name in the params section to provide type annotations for args and options defined in the params section. A value is a plain type such as `int`, optionally with a default (`int = 5`), or a complete definition: `str = typer.Option(...)` for Typer, a decorator such as `@click.option(...)` for Click. |
| `global_params` | list of [params](#params) | `[]` | Parameters applied to all commands |
| `command_templates` | mapping of name to [CommandTemplate](#commandtemplate) | `{}` | Reusable command templates |
| `commands` | mapping of name to ([Command](#command), string or list of strings) or list of [Command](#command) | `{}` | The commands of the CLI, keyed by name. In a key, `.` separates groups, `\|` separates aliases and a leading `(*)` adds the command to every group. |
| `callbacks` | list of [Callback](#callback) | `[]` | Code that runs before any command of the CLI, or of one command group. Callbacks for the same target run in the order given and their params are combined. The built-in --version and --aliases options are kept. |
| `cli_options` | mapping | `{}` | Additional CLI configuration options |
| `tests` | list of (string or mapping of name to string) | `[]` | Test cases for commands |
| `examples` | list of (string or [Example](#example)) | `[]` | Example command lines of the CLI, with an optional description each. Shown at the end of the `--help` of the generated CLI and in the pages written by `cli docs`. |

- `name` and `version` are the only required keys. `version` must be a string, so quote values such as
  `"1.0"`. `commands` can be left out for a CLI that only has `callbacks`.
- Unknown top-level keys are ignored.
- `manifestVersion` can be left out. A value other than `v3` stops the load with an error that says
  what to change. This also applies to include files and to files written in a blueprint's spec.
- `vars` keys must be valid Python identifiers. A value is a string, a number, a boolean, or a one-key
  mapping such as `{os.getcwd()}`, which is emitted as a Python expression. See
  [Vars and Jinja](../guides/vars-and-jinja.md).
- `cli_options` is passed as keyword arguments to `typer.Typer(...)`, or to `click.group(...)` when
  `use_click` is set. Useful Typer values are `add_completion: false` and `no_args_is_help: true`.
- `commands` is usually a mapping. A list of [Command](#command) mappings that each set `name` is also
  accepted.
- Each `tests` entry is either a string starting with `$` or `>` (a shell step) or a one-key mapping of
  command line to assertion code. See [Testing manifests](../guides/testing.md).

## Command

Defines a single command within the CLI. It specifies the command's execution logic, parameters, and configuration.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | string or list of strings | `""` | The script to run. A string, or a list of strings that are joined with newlines. Lines starting with `$` or `>` are shell commands. |
| `help` | string | `""` | A description of the command, displayed in the help output. |
| `params` | list of [params](#params) | `[]` | The parameters of the command. Each entry takes one of three forms: a shorthand mapping of the param name to its type, such as `name: str!` or `--count: int = 1`; an explicit mapping with the keys `name` and `type` and optionally `default`, `help`, `short` and `required`; or a string that is copied into the generated code as written (a signature entry for Typer, a decorator for Click). |
| `template` | string | `""` | A reference to a command template defined in the `command_templates` section of the manifest. This allows for reusable command definitions. |
| `pre_run` | string | `""` | Script to run before the command's run block. This can be used for setup tasks or preconditions. |
| `post_run` | string | `""` | Script to run after the command's run block. This can be used for cleanup tasks or post-processing. |
| `aliases` | list of strings | `[]` | A list of aliases for the command. These aliases can be used to invoke the command with a different name. |
| `name` | string | `""` | The name of the command. This is generally derived from the key in the `commands` section of the manifest, but can be explicitly set here. |
| `config` | [CommandConfig](#commandconfig) or null | `null` | An optional `CommandConfig` object that provides additional configuration options for the command, such as context settings, help text customization, and visibility. |

A command value can also be just a string or a list of strings, which is shorthand for a mapping with
only `run`.

The key of the command carries meaning: `.` separates groups (`db.create`), `|` separates aliases
(`delete|rm`) and a leading `(*)` adds the command to every group. See
[Commands, groups and aliases](../guides/commands.md).

A command that has `help` and no `run`, and whose key is the name of a group, sets the help text of
that group.

## Params

Every entry of a `params` list (on a command, a template or `global_params`) takes one of three forms.

### Shorthand

A one-key mapping: the key is the name, the value is the type.

| Part | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Positional argument | `source: str` |
| `--name` | Option | `--count: int` |
| `--name|-n` | Option with a short alias | `--count|-c: int` |
| `type!` | Required | `source: str!` |
| `type = value` | Default value, written as a Python expression | `target: str = "out.txt"` |
| a name from `types` | Reuse a type or a full definition | `level: Level` |

Hyphens in a name become underscores in the Python variable (`--dry-run` is `dry_run`).

### Explicit

A mapping with the keys of [CommandParam](#commandparam), which adds `help` text.

### Generic

A plain string that is copied into the generated function signature as written, for example
`'lines: int = typer.Option(10, "--lines", "-n", min=1)'`. With the Click backend the string is a
decorator such as `"@click.option('--loud', is_flag=True)"`.

See [Params and types](../guides/params.md) for worked examples of all three.

## CommandParam

Defines the structure of a command parameter. It is used within the `params` field of a `Command` object. By default, parameters are treated as positional arguments. To specify an option, prefix the name with `--` to indicate flag.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **required** | Parameter name. Prefix with `--` to indicate an option. |
| `type` | string | **required** | Parameter type (e.g., 'str', 'int', 'bool', or a custom type defined in the manifest's 'types' section). |
| `default` | any | `null` | Default parameter value. |
| `help` | string | `""` | Parameter description. |
| `short` | string | `""` | Short option alias. i.e. '-v' for verbose. |
| `required` | boolean | `false` | Whether the parameter is required. |

This is the explicit form. A `name` without `--` is a positional argument, with both backends. `short`
is written with its dash (`-w`). A `str` default is quoted for you; other defaults are emitted as
written.

## CommandTemplate

Defines a reusable template for command definitions. Templates allow you to define common parameters, pre-run/post-run scripts, and configuration options that can be applied to multiple commands.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `params` | list of [params](#params) | `[]` | A list of parameters for the command template. These parameters will be applied to any command that uses this template. |
| `pre_run` | string | `""` | Script to run before the command's run and pre-run block. This script will be applied to any command that uses this template. |
| `post_run` | string | `""` | Script to run after the command's run and post-run block. This script will be applied to any command that uses this template. |
| `config` | [CommandConfig](#commandconfig) or null | `null` | Additional configuration options for commands using this template. This allows customization of help text, context settings, and other Typer command parameters. |

Template `params` are placed before the command's own params. Scripts run in this order: template
`pre_run`, command `pre_run`, command `run`, command `post_run`, template `post_run`. `config` values
from the command override the template's. See
[Command templates and global params](../guides/templates-and-global-params.md).

## CommandConfig

Configuration options for a Cliffy command.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context_settings` | mapping | `{}` | Settings passed to the Click context of the command, for example `help_option_names` or `max_content_width`. |
| `epilog` | string | `""` | Text displayed after the help message. |
| `short_help` | string | `""` | Short one-line help message displayed in help overviews. |
| `options_metavar` | string | `"[OPTIONS]"` | Placeholder text displayed for options in help messages. |
| `add_help_option` | boolean | `true` | Whether to add the `--help` option automatically. |
| `no_args_is_help` | boolean | `false` | If True, invoking the command without any arguments displays the help message. |
| `hidden` | boolean | `false` | If True, the command is hidden from help messages and command lists. |
| `deprecated` | boolean | `false` | If True, the command is marked as deprecated in help messages. |
| `rich_help_panel` | string | `""` | Name of the panel this command is listed under in rich help output. |

Only the keys you set are passed on, as keyword arguments of the `command()` decorator of Typer or
Click. With the Click backend `rich_help_panel` needs rich-click.

## Callback

Code that runs before the commands of the CLI, or of one command group. A callback can declare its own params, which become options of the CLI (or group) itself, i.e. `mycli --verbose command`. The Typer/Click context is available in the run block as `ctx`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | string | **required** | Code to run before the invoked command. `ctx` holds the context. |
| `group` | string | `""` | Command group the callback belongs to, i.e. `db` or `db.tables`. Leave empty for the CLI itself. |
| `params` | list of [params](#params) | `[]` | Params of the CLI (or group) itself, given before the command name. Same syntax as command params. |
| `invoke_without_command` | boolean | `false` | Also run the callback when the CLI (or group) is invoked without a command, instead of showing the help. |

Callbacks for the same target run in the order given. Their params are options of the CLI or group
itself, so they go before the command name: `mycli --verbose db migrate`. A `group` must be the name of
an existing command group. See [Callbacks](../blueprints.md#callbacks).

## Example

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | string | **required** | The command line to show. |
| `description` | string or null | `null` | A sentence describing what the command does. |

`examples` entries are shown at the end of the `--help` of the generated CLI, as
`$ <command>  # <description>`, and in the pages written by [`cli docs`](../guides/generating-docs.md).
An entry can also be a plain string, which is shown without a description.

## Include files

Special model specifically to define the allowed named objects that can be merged with other manifests.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requires` | list of strings | `[]` | Merged into the `requires` of the including manifest. |
| `commands` | mapping of name to ([Command](#command), string or list of strings) | `{}` | Merged into the `commands` of the including manifest. |
| `vars` | mapping of name to (string or `{expression}`) | `{}` | Merged into `vars`. Available as Python variables, not as `{{ }}` placeholders. |
| `imports` | string or list of strings | `[]` | Merged into `imports`. |
| `functions` | list of strings | `[]` | Merged into `functions`. Must be a list here. |
| `types` | mapping of name to string | `{}` | Merged into `types`. |
| `cli_options` | mapping of name to string | `{}` | Merged into `cli_options`. |
| `tests` | list of (string or mapping of name to string) | `[]` | Appended to `tests`. |

Files listed under `includes` are validated against this smaller model. A relative path is looked up
next to the including manifest first, then in the directory you run `cli` from. See
[Includes and merging](../guides/includes.md).

<!-- docs/project/known-issues.md -->

# Known issues

Behavior in cliffy 0.7.1 that differs from what you might expect, with the way around each. Every
item was reproduced against this release. The guides already recommend the forms that work; this
page explains why.

## Commands

### Some problems are only found by `cli validate` and `cli test`

Every command checks the scripts of a manifest and reports a syntax error with its command, line and
column. A problem that only shows when the generated code is imported is not found by `cli load`,
`cli render` or `cli build`: a type name that does not exist, or params that do not fit together in
one signature. The CLI is then loaded or built and fails when it is started.

**Do this instead:** run `cli validate` first. It imports the generated code and reports such a
problem against the command it comes from.

### `cli test` does not check shell steps

A `$` or `>` step that exits with an error does not fail the run. A step whose program does not
exist ends the run with an error message. See [Testing manifests](../guides/testing.md#things-to-know).

### Examples are shown for the CLI, not per command

`examples` belongs to the manifest. The generated CLI shows all of them at the end of its own
`--help`; the help of a single command has no examples section, because a command has no `examples`
key. With the Typer backend an example that contains an emoji code such as `:rocket:` is shown as
the emoji, like the rest of the help text.

### `cli remove` refuses when the launcher was changed

The launcher of a loaded CLI is only deleted while it is exactly the file cliffy wrote. After an
edit, or when another program replaced it, `cli remove` and `cli remove-all` remove nothing for that
CLI and exit with 1.

**Do this instead:** move or delete the file named in the message, then run `cli remove` again.

### A file can still appear between cliffy's check and its write

cliffy checks a launcher right before it replaces or deletes it, never follows a symbolic link and
creates a new launcher only when nothing has the name. Replacing or deleting an existing launcher
is a check followed by a rename or an unlink: a file that another process puts at exactly that path
in between is replaced or removed. This needs write access to the environment's `bin` directory at
that moment.

## Manifests

### Includes fall back to the working directory

An include path is looked up next to the including manifest first. When it is not found there, it is
looked up in the directory `cli` is run from, so the same manifest can pick up a different file
depending on where you are.

**Do this instead:** keep include files next to (or below) the manifest that lists them.

### A full Typer definition in `types` replaces the param's own settings

A `types` entry with `typer.Option(...)` or `typer.Argument(...)` is the complete definition. A
default, `help` or `short` written on a param that uses it is ignored, and `cli validate` warns
about it. Plain types such as `Count: int` do not have this effect. See [Params and types](../guides/params.md#types).

## Click backend

`use_click: true` supports every manifest feature. Generic params and full definitions in `types`
are written as Click decorators instead of Typer expressions. The details are in
[Click and Typer backends](../guides/backends.md#what-differs-from-typer).
